title: Not drinking, smoking or socializing; reared to be a lady
summary: Other entertainers called her swell-headed because she did not sit in bars; her grandmother and mother taught her to respect herself.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: Yes. You haven't described the De Luxe. You said there was a billiard parlor downstairs.
Yeah. Well, of course I used to just go upstairs and do my work and come on downstairs. I was
never much of a -- I didn't drink.

I didn't smoke. And I didn't socialize much. I always -- they used to call me and say I was swell headed, and I thought I was better than the rest of the entertainers, because I didn't sit around in bars and things. I just -- I was reared by an old, old, old lady, what rearing I had, when I was at home. And I was always told by my grandmother, and my mother, to be a lady, always respect yourself and you can demand respect. So I was always to myself.
Well, you obviously didn't forget that.
You obviously did not forget that.
Oh, thank you. More or less I stayed to myself.
